study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities unveil two neuroanatomical obsessive-compulsive disorder subtypes

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states objectives to delineate OCD subtypes using individualized gray matter morphological differences derived from normative models. It also states secondary objectives to assess reproducibility and to relate subtype abnormalities to normal brain network architecture and neurotransmitter receptor/transporter distributions. These satisfy the criteria that research questions are provided and the purpose of applying normative modeling is described.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Our study aimed to delineate OCD subtypes based on individualized gray matter morphological differences. ... Utilizing normative models of gray matter volume, we identified subtypes..." ... "we investigated their associations with normal brain network architecture and the distribution of neurotransmitter receptors/transporters."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: For a new model, the study reports the healthy control sample size (106 HCs) and specifies that image quality was recorded via the Image Quality Rating (IQR). However, explicit eligibility/inclusion and exclusion criteria for HCs and reasons for exclusion are not described in the available text.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We recruited 100 untreated, first-episode OCD patients and 106 healthy controls for structural imaging scans." ... "To ensure data quality, the Image Quality Rating (IQR) was recorded."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are explicitly modeled as covariates when training the normative model on healthy controls. The data appear to be single-site, so multi-site harmonization is not applicable.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "we trained a Gaussian process regression model to estimate the normative range of regional GMVs from age and sex in HCs"

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The study indicates primary data collection with a specific scanner model (3T GE Discovery MR750), implying a single-site dataset. However, it does not explicitly detail the collection site(s) and time period for the HC reference cohort.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "High-resolution T1-weighted anatomical images ... 3-Tesla GE Discovery MR750 scanner (General Electric, ...)."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Primary data collection is described with modality (T1-weighted MRI), detailed acquisition parameters (TR, TE, TI, flip angle, matrix, slices, thickness, voxel size), and equipment (GE Discovery MR750, 3T).
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "High-resolution T1-weighted anatomical images ... 3-Tesla GE Discovery MR750 ... parameters: repetition time = 8164 ms, echo time = 3.18 ms, inversion time = 900 ms, flip angle = 7 degrees, resolution matrix = 256 × 256, slices = 188, thickness = 1.0 mm and voxel size = 1 × 1 × 1 mm³."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described using CAT12 voxel-based morphometry with standard steps (bias-field correction, tissue segmentation, partial volume correction, normalization to MNI, resampling, modulation, smoothing). Quality control via IQR is noted, and TIV is computed.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Voxel-wise gray matter volume (GMV) ... using voxel-based morphometry in the CAT12 toolbox ... bias-field correction, brain segmentation ... correction for partial volume effects, normalization to MNI ... resampling to 1.5 mm³, and nonlinear modulation. Subsequently ... smoothing with a 6-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel. Additionally, the total intracranial volume (TIV) ... To ensure data quality, the Image Quality Rating (IQR) was recorded."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: For the new normative model, there is no description of a data partitioning strategy (e.g., hold-out set, K-fold, LOOCV) where the model is tested on samples not used for fitting. The methods outline model training and downstream analyses without mentioning internal validation on unseen HCs.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "we trained a Gaussian process regression model ... [on HCs] ... This trained model was then applied to each patient ..." (no mention of cross-validation/hold-out for HCs).

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study does not report applying the trained normative model to an independent external healthy dataset separate from the development cohort.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: The methods describe training on local HCs and application to patients; no external HC dataset is described.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical model is specified as Gaussian process regression with inputs age and sex to predict regional GMVs per a connectome atlas, and Z-scores quantify deviations. However, key model settings (e.g., kernel type, priors) and software/libraries are not specified.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "we trained a Gaussian process regression model to estimate the normative range of regional GMVs from age and sex in HCs according to the brain connectome atlas ... Subsequently, Z scores were calculated to quantify deviations ..."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: No quantitative metrics of model fit or calibration on the reference cohort (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, coverage) are reported in the available methods/results.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: The normative modeling paragraph describes training and generating Z-scores but does not report performance metrics on HCs.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning of the reference cohort is described for the new model; therefore, characteristics per partition are not applicable per the guide's branching.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: No train/validation/test partitions of HCs are described in methods.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Reproducibility information includes software/tools and a specific version for the GPR library (GPML Toolbox v4.2) with URLs; CAT12 and SPM12 are cited; and a Python toolbox for dominance analysis is linked. However, availability of the trained models and the imaging data is not stated.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "Gray matter volume is assessed with the Computational Anatomy Toolbox (CAT12, http://dbm.neuro.uni-jena.de/cat12/). The normative model is freely available (GAUSSIAN PROCESS REGRESSION AND CLASSIFICATION Toolbox version 4.2, http://www.GaussianProcess.org/gpml/code). Group-level differences in GMV are obtained using SPM12 ... Dominance analysis is performed with python toolbox (https://github.com/kaladharprajapati/dominance_analysis)."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Primary data collection is indicated with 100 first-episode, untreated OCD patients and quality control noted via IQR. However, detailed diagnostic criteria (e.g., DSM/ICD), explicit inclusion/exclusion, and reasons for exclusion are not described in the available text.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "We recruited 100 first-episode, untreated patients diagnosed with OCD ..." ... "To ensure data quality, the Image Quality Rating (IQR) was recorded."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses involving deviation scores and subtype comparisons mention adjustments for basic demographics and TIV, but there is no evidence that clinical covariates beyond demographics (e.g., medication, illness duration, symptom severity) were modeled in deviation analyses.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "two-sample t-test, with sex, age, and TIV as covariates."

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Primary data collection is implied with a specific scanner and local recruitment, but collection sites and time period are not fully described in the available text.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "High-resolution T1-weighted ... acquired using ... GE Discovery MR750 ..."; authors affiliated with The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University.

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Clinical characteristics are reported, including sample sizes, demographics (sex, age), and clinical measures (Y-BOCS, illness duration, age of onset), at least by subtype in Supplementary Table S1.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: Table S1: "Subtype 1 (N = 49) ... Subtype 2 (N = 51) ... Male ... Age ... Y-BOCS ... Illness duration ... Age of onset ..."

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: The clinical measure Y-BOCS is specified, but assessment procedures (e.g., structured interview, rater type) are not described in the available text.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The meaning and direction of deviation (Z) scores are clearly explained (positive indicates higher GMV than normative, negative indicates lower). Quantitative thresholds for categorization are not reported, and clinical implications are discussed at a high level via subtype characterization rather than explicit clinical relationships or thresholds.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "Z scores were calculated to quantify deviations ... Positive Z scores indicated higher GMVs in patients compared to HCs, and vice versa."
